doc.title: Danny Barker Interview (Louis Armstrong memorial broadcast), 1971-07-09

title: Armstrong as New Orleans king and Oscar Cohen's tribute as road manager
summary: A New Orleans speaker tells of Armstrong's Rex toast to the King of England, followed by Oscar Cohen recalling being his road manager and his influence.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: We're real proud of the fact that he was born and raised in New Orleans. The central figure in the Mardi Gras here in New Orleans is King Rex, who is the king of the parade on Mardi Gras Day, the Rex parade. So when Louis Armstrong had an opportunity to play for royalty in England, he addressed the royal box, the king and the queen of England. When he was ready to play his last tune, the saints go marching in. And he said to the king, he said, this next number is for you, Rex. That gives you an idea of the kind of a man he was. He was very happy, hardworking, and as I say, the greatest stylist on the instrument that I've ever heard, and perhaps the greatest man for jazz that I've certainly known in my lifetime. I was Louis Armstrong when I was 15 years old, When I was an office boy at Associated Booking Corporation. I was his road manager, who about seven years later, He was the kindest human being I've ever met in my life. He was always happy, and he wanted everyone else to be happy around him. And it was the most pleasant three or four months I spent in my life. Only last Thursday, Louis called me and said to me, Oscar, you got to come out to the house. Take a look at me and you'll see how great I look. And in two weeks of rehearsals, I'll be ready to work. Of course, this tragic event happened. And I'm sure Louis knows how much the world loves him. Louis Armstrong, I think, has influenced every musician and singer. In the past 40 years, I think that they all have, Somewhere along the way, have been influenced by Louis Armstrong. It's the end of an era of this great man. Because I'm sure in 50 years from now, or 20 years from now, Or 100 years from now, he'll be in every history book. And every child will have read about Louis Armstrong in any school, In any part of the world. He was just the greatest. He was just the greatest.
